claims.text: Pre-excited AF, hemodynamically stable: ibutilide or IV procainamide = beneficial.
claims.quote: Ibutilide or intravenous procainamide is beneficial for acute treatment in patients with pre-excited AF who are hemodynamically stable.

claims.text: Stable wide-complex (antidromic) tachy after failed vagal maneuvers: IV procainamide, IV amiodarone or synchronized cardioversion.
claims.quote: If stable and vagal maneuvers are unsuccessful, therapy with IV procainamide, IV amiodarone, or synchronized cardioversion is recommended

claims.text: AF + WPW: ⍉digoxin, adenosine or NDHP CCBs (may trigger VF).
claims.quote: Do not give digoxin, adenosine, or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil, diltiazem) to patients with atrial fibrillation and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome because these medications may trigger ventricular fibrillation.
